questions.q: A component is created with the camelCase name `contactCard`. How is it referenced inside another component's markup?
options: <contactCard></contactCard>
<lightning-contact-card></lightning-contact-card>
<c:contactCard></c:contactCard>
<c-contact-card></c-contact-card>
questions.explain: In markup, a component's camelCase name is converted to kebab-case and prefixed with the namespace -- `c` by default for components created in your own org -- giving `<c-contact-card>`.

questions.q: Which three files does every LWC component bundle require, per this lesson and Lesson 1?
options: `.css`, `.svg`, and `__tests__`
`.json`, `.html`, and `.css`
`.js`, `.html`, and `.js-meta.xml`
`.js`, `.svg`, and `__tests__`
questions.explain: The `.js`, `.html`, and `.js-meta.xml` files are required in every bundle. The `.css` file, the `.svg` icon, and the `__tests__` folder are all optional.

questions.q: What does the `__tests__` folder inside a component bundle actually get used for?
options: It holds Jest test files for local or CI testing and is never deployed to a Salesforce org
It is deployed to the org and used to generate App Builder documentation
It stores a backup copy of the component's `.js-meta.xml` file
It is required for a component to be exposed in Lightning App Builder
questions.explain: The `__tests__` folder holds Jest unit tests for the component. It exists purely for local and CI testing and is never deployed to a Salesforce org.

questions.q: What happens to a component whose `.js-meta.xml` leaves `isExposed` set to `false` (or omitted, since that's the default)?
options: It cannot be used anywhere at all, including as a child of another component
It is automatically deployed with a default icon and shown in every App Builder page
It can still be used as a child inside other components in the same project, but it will never appear in Lightning App Builder, Experience Builder, or as a standalone tab
It can only be used inside Apex classes, never inside other LWC components
questions.explain: `isExposed` defaults to `false`. A component left this way can still be nested as a child inside other components, but it won't show up as a choice for admins building pages in App Builder or Experience Builder.

questions.q: In the `caseList` / `caseRow` example from this lesson, what does the `apiVersion` element in a component's `.js-meta.xml` control?
options: Which Salesforce org the component is allowed to deploy to
Whether the component's CSS file is scoped or global
The Salesforce API version the component is pinned to, which affects which newer directives and features are available to it
Whether the component can call Apex methods imperatively
questions.explain: `apiVersion` pins a component to a specific Salesforce API version, which determines which newer template directives and platform features that component can use.
